Thanks Lauren — attaching the initial artifacts.

Included in this message:  
- Attachment: redwood_scim_sample_delta.ndjson (NDJSON, 3 days: 2026-07-06T00:00Z to 2026-07-08T23:59Z) — contains events with timestamp, operation (create/update/deactivate), externalId, and prior state diffs redacted to user identifiers only.
- Attachment: saml_attribute_mapping.csv (CSV) — shows IdP attributes we map to our internal identity, and the SP NameID format used by Redwood.
- Short attestation (pasted below) on least-privilege controls for tenant-scoped resources.

Attestation (brief):
Redwood enforces least privilege for tenant-scoped resources via role-based access controls and scoped service accounts. Administrative actions are gated by RBAC roles defined at the account and project level; default roles are read-only for new service tokens. All privileged operations (instance resize, key export, tenant-level user administration) require an elevated role and are logged. SCIM provisioning applies attribute-based filters and supports group-to-role mappings so that identity provider group membership determines the assigned role. Access reviews are performed quarterly and evidence of reviews is retained in our audit logs. This attestation is accurate to the best of my knowledge as of 2026-08-26.

Next steps: I will produce a RBAC role export for HealthBridge and a brief mapping from RBAC role -> permitted actions (CSV) by EOD today.

Olga Petrov
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
